newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - December 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - December 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
THE GUARDIAN
-- SECRET PLAN TO SPLIT BAT FAILS

A plan to split the tobacco and financial services group, BAT Industries, has failed. The plan would have involved the merger of BAT's financial business, which includes Allied Dunbar and Eagle Star in the UK, with one of Britain's other leading insurance groups. Lazard Brothers, the merchant bank, and stockbroker Cazenove are known to have been working on the deal, which would have transformed Britain's insurance sector.
-- TREASURY RAISES 257 MILLION STG IN SALE OF RESIDUAL GOVERNMENT STAKES

The Treasury has collected 257 million stg towards Budget tax cuts when it sold most of the government's remaining stakes in privatised businesses, such as British Energy, National Grid and Scottish Power. The sell-off means that the Government has completed its 1.5 billion stg "mop-up privatisation", aimed at selling residual holdings in privatised companies ahead of the general election.
-- CHANCELLOR'S ADVISOR TALKS DOWN INFLATION

According to Alan Budd, a senior Treasury economist, the Bank of England is too pessimistic about the outlook for inflation. He suggested that Chancellor Kenneth Clarke will resist pressure to raise interest rates when he meets Eddie George, the bank's governor, next week. He told a Commons Treasury Select Committee that the economy could grow at above trend for two years without threatening low, stable inflation.
THE TIMES
-- LUCASVARITY SHAKE-UP WILL HIT 8,000 JOBS

The Anglo-American automotive components group, LucasVarity, has announced that its efforts to reduce costs will mean the loss of 3,000 jobs worldwide in the next two years. Businesses employing a further 5,000 people are to be sold. The restructuring will give rise to total exceptional charges of 250 million stg. The company was unable to say how many of the cuts will fall in the UK.
-- MCDONNELL DOUGLAS LINK-UP WITH BOEING THREATENS AIRBUS

Boeing and the American commercial aircraft manufacturer McDonnell Douglas have agreed to a collaboration on Boeing jet programmes in a deal that could pose a serious challenge to Boeing's European rival Airbus Industrie. The first project McDonnell Douglas will join is the development of two new versions of the 747 jumbo jet and the co-operation is likely to broaden. This will herald the creation of a new powerful force in aircraft manufacturing.
-- TWO DOGS UNLEASHES SURPRISE BUYER

The Australian alcopops company Two Dogs has sold out to Pernod Ricard, the French drinks group, for 9.7 million stg. The sale will make owner and managing director Duncan MacGillivray a multimillionaire. The drink is sold in 44 countries and last year had worldwide sales of around 60 million Australian dollars. The sale means that MacGillivry, who still owns 70 percent of Two Dogs, has turned a 500,000 investment into 14 million Australian dollars.
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- DORLING SUFFERS AS POUND STAYS STRONG

Shares in the print and publishing group Dorling Kindersley plunged after a warning that profits are being hit by sterling's strength against the dollar. Company chairman and chief executive Peter Kindersley also warned that it is experiencing "softer conditions" in the book publishing market in the US. He said trading conditions in Dorling Kindersley's American multimedia division have continued to be difficult although the company is trading well in Britain.
-- GOLD SLUMPS TO THREE-YEAR LOW

The price of gold has fallen to its lowest level in more than three years. Dealers blamed the rise in the dollar, which increases the cost of buying bullion with other currencies. Gold has fallen steadily through this year from a peak of more than 400 dollars an ounce and some traders forecast that it could continue to slide to about 362 and a half dollars. The market has been hit by rumours of a central bank that was selling reserves as well as mining houses disposing of stock and there was very little buying demand.
-- 'BLACK BELT' SQUAD TO SAVE SIEBE 50 MILLION STG

One of Britain's biggest engineering companies Siebe have announced plans to boost profits by 50 million stg a year by training a squad of 200 staff to eliminate defects in products, designs, and customer service. Allen Yurko, chief executive, said Siebe will adopt a quality control programme called Six Sigma, developed by an American management consulting company. He said 200 staff will be trained as "black belts" in statistical techniques and will be employed across the group's 150 companies to spot errors.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- INSIDER DEALING JURY FAILS TO REACH VERDICT

The jury have failed to reach a verdict in the insider dealing trial of the former director of strategy at Eastern Electricity, Douglas Swinden. He is to face a retrial in the new year if authorities decide to pursue the case but doubts have arisen about whether it will go ahead. It has also emerged that in the wake of this setback a conviction has been secured in the case of Geoffrey Atkinson and John Hawksby in another insider trading case.
-- UNITED AIRLINES STEPS UP ATTACK ON ALLIANCE

The world's largest airline, United Airlines, has stepped up its attack on the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines as officials from the UK and US governments resume their "open skies" negotiations aimed at liberalising access to Heathrow airport. The outcome of the talks could determine whether the US regulatory authorities will give the partnership their approval. The US government has already said it will approve the alliance if the UK frees up access to Heathrow.
-- RACAL MOVES TO CALM FEARS WITH NEWS OF TWO BILLION STG LINK-UP

Following Monday's profits warning Racal Electronics has sought to stem shareholder discontent by announcing it will bid for a two million stg British army radio contract by agreeing to join with a rival defence consortium. The company's chairman, Sir Ernest Harrison, has failed to discount speculation that he is considering retirement.
